rationale.summary: Vote: ABSTAIN. For this NewCommittee (active), evidence quality was insufficient for a reliable YES or NO decision. Primary blocker: DRep distribution signal was unavailable for this action. Decisive reason: if claims cannot be tied to replayable evidence, abstaining avoids overclaiming certainty. Weighed against it: the proposal substantiates "This governance action updates the four Constitutional Committee seats whose terms expire at the end of Epoch 653 by appointing the candidates elected through the 2026 Constitutional Committee election." and clears the evidence gates. What would enable a directional vote: Provide mitigation evidence; Provide independent assurance. Residual uncertainty: No DRep distribution available. Confidence context: score 0.05; confidence 66.2%.

sections.conclusion: Baseline fields and source anchors establish whether the proposal can be reviewed at all.

sections.title: Claims and evidence
findings: Proposal document read by reasoning layer: yes
Stated amount: not stated in document

Deliverables: This governance action updates the four Constitutional Committee seats whose terms expire at the end of Epoch 653 by appointing the candidates elected through the 2026 Constitutional Committee election., The successful candidates will serve new terms ending at Epoch 799, in accordance with the current committeeMaxTermLength protocol parameter., The Constitutional Committee must be renewed as members' terms expire to maintain a functioning committee at or above the minimum size required by the committeeMinSize protocol parameter., This action replaces the four seats expiring at Epoch 653 with the candidates elected by the community through the 2026 Constitutional Committee election, facilitated by Intersect.

Claim (governance, independently_verifiable, high materiality): This governance action updates the four Constitutional Committee seats whose terms expire at the end of Epoch 653 by appointing the candidates elected through the 2026 Constitutional Committee election.

Claim (technical, independently_verifiable, high materiality): The successful candidates will serve new terms ending at Epoch 799, in accordance with the current committeeMaxTermLength protocol parameter.

Claim (technical, independently_verifiable, high materiality): The Constitutional Committee must be renewed as members' terms expire to maintain a functioning committee at or above the minimum size required by the committeeMinSize protocol parameter.

Claim (governance, independently_verifiable, high materiality): This action replaces the four seats expiring at Epoch 653 with the candidates elected by the community through the 2026 Constitutional Committee election, facilitated by Intersect.

Claim (governance, independently_verifiable, medium materiality): The election included candidate registration, a public voting period, an independent audit of the results, and publication of the audited outcome before submission of this governance action.

Claim (governance, independently_verifiable, high materiality): In accordance with the Cardano constitution, Article III, Section 3 (2), Intersect has facilitated a public “process… for \[the\] election of members of the CC consistent with the requirements of the Guardrails”, to update the positions due to expire at Epo...
sections.conclusion: Each claim must map to replayable public evidence; proposer assertions alone are not enough for confidence.

sections.title: Risk review
sections.conclusion: Risk is not a side note; unmitigated execution or governance risk can dominate an otherwise attractive proposal.

sections.title: Counterargument pass
findings: Strongest YES: the proposal substantiates "This governance action updates the four Constitutional Committee seats whose terms expire at the end of Epoch 653 by appointing the candidates elected through the 2026 Constitutional Committee election." and clears the evidence gates.
Strongest NO: weak controls, unclear delivery, or governance precedent could outweigh the benefit of NewCommittee.
Strongest hold: if claims cannot be tied to replayable evidence, abstaining avoids overclaiming certainty.
sections.conclusion: A defensible rationale must show the best opposing case before it reaches a vote.

sections.title: Synthesis
findings: Final vote must be derived from completed sections above, not from a prose summary.
The public rationale should name the decisive section and the strongest counterargument.
sections.conclusion: The vote is only credible if the assessment tree shows enough work for a skeptical delegator to audit.
